# Code of conduct

## The short version

Be decent. Assume the other person is trying to help.

## What that means here

This is a small project with a small number of people in it. The things that actually go wrong
in a repository this size are not dramatic, so this document is about those rather than about
hypotheticals.

**In issues.** Somebody reporting a bug is doing you a favour, including when the report is
thin. Ask for what is missing rather than closing it. Somebody asking for a feature that will
not be built gets a reason, not silence.

**In pull requests.** Review the change, not the person. "This will break on ESX because the
identifier is the character key" is a review; "this is wrong" is not. A contributor who has read
RULES.md and still got something wrong found a gap in RULES.md.

**About other resources.** This resource compares itself to Advanced Parking in its own
documentation because that is the thing people are choosing between, and it does so factually.
Do not use this repository to run down somebody else's work, paid or free. Kiminaze's
VehicleDeformation is MIT and is credited in the code that learned from it; that is the standard.

**About servers.** Nobody's server configuration is stupid. A server with a fifteen-thousand
vehicle table and a two-year-old qb-core fork is a server that has been running for two years.

## Not acceptable

Harassment, personal attacks, discriminatory language, deliberately derailing a thread, and
publishing anybody's private information. Any of those gets the comment removed and, if it
continues, the account blocked from the repository.

## Reporting

Open a private security advisory from the **Security** tab, which is the only private channel
this repository has. It reaches the maintainer and nobody else.

## Scope

This applies to issues, pull requests, discussions and commit messages in this repository.
